reading.body:
Cindy Hyde-Smith's AI record is one cosponsorship, thirteen recorded votes on a single bill, and two Amazon PAC contributions of $2,500 each.

The votes cluster on S. 2296, which drew eleven recorded votes on September 2, September 10, and October 9, 2025. She voted Yea on cloture, on the motion to proceed, on the motion to table an amendment, and on passage, and split across the eight amendment votes on October 9. The only other legislative item is a March 19, 2026 cosponsorship of S. 4154, the Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026. The two Amazon PAC contributions are dated March 28, 2025 and June 24, 2026, both at $2,500.

For AI specifically, this is a thin record. One AI-named bill cosponsored, and a set of votes on a bill whose AI content the data does not describe. Nothing here ties the contributions to the votes, and the page states that placement in date order is not a claim of causation. The data also does not say what S. 2296 does, whether the amendment votes concerned AI, or whether any other AI legislation moved through committee without a recorded vote.

What the record does show is the shape of a junior senator's AI footprint: mostly party-line procedural voting on one vehicle, plus sustained PAC money from a company whose data center and power buildout is the subject this site tracks. The contributions are small and identical, which is consistent with a routine giving pattern rather than a targeted push. The data cannot distinguish those.
